diagnosis.summary: Nightly ingest for 2026-10-01 failed because upstream now sends orders.order_total with a "$" prefix (e.g. "$4.99"). The DECIMAL(12,2) cast fails on that. Proposed fix: set the strip_currency parser on orders.order_total, as the schema-change runbook prescribes, then rerun.

root_cause.explanation: The 2026-10-01 orders.csv has order_total formatted with a leading '$'. The 2026-09-30 file had plain numerics. The headers are unchanged, and the ingest config has no parser, so the DECIMAL cast fails. The meaning is unchanged (USD), so it is safe to adapt at ingest.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed on casting '$4.99' to DECIMAL(12,2) for order_total

The 10-01 file has a '$' prefix on order_total in the sampled rows; the 09-30 file has plain numbers; headers are identical. Only the first three rows and the last row were sampled, so I did not confirm that every row has the prefix.
No parser is configured at ingest
The runbook prescribes set_column_parser with strip_currency for reformatted values, and says redelivery is wrong for a persistent upstream change

alternatives_considered: request_upstream_redelivery: rejected, because a persistent format change would just reproduce the '$' values
rerun_only: rejected, because the file is unchanged and the cast would fail again
revert_model_change: rejected, because the failure is at ingest and no dbt model is implicated

escalate: not needed, because the runbook gives a safe allow-listed fix. The ~4.6% row-count drop (440 vs 461) with continuous order IDs looks like normal variation, but verify row counts and revenue after the rerun.

proposal.rationale: Upstream now sends order_total with a "$" prefix; meaning unchanged (USD). Runbook prescribes strip_currency parser at ingest. Row count drop of ~4.6% is within normal range and IDs are continuous.

applied: ingest now parses raw.orders.order_total with strip_currency
